units.title: Saying things
units.goal: Make your program show words and numbers.
pages: Your first instruction
`say` shows something in the Output. Text goes in double quotes. Numbers don't need quotes, and Flaux works out sums before showing them.

say "Hello, world!"
say 42
say 2 + 2
Several things at once
Give `say` several things separated by commas. They're shown on one line, with a space between each. Brackets are fine too: `say("hi")`.

say "Score:", 10
say("Lives:", 3, "Level:", 2)
Staying on the same line
`say` finishes its line, so the next thing starts on a new one. `say.same` doesn't: the next thing said goes right after it. It adds exactly what you give it, so put the spaces in yourself.

say.same "Loading"
say.same "..."
say " done!"
Notes for people
Everything after `#` on a line is a comment: Flaux skips it. Use comments to explain your code.

# This line is skipped
say "This one runs"   # and this note is skipped too

units.title: Variables
units.goal: Keep values in named boxes and change them.
pages: A name for a value
A variable is a name that holds a value. Make one with `set ... to ...`, and use its name wherever you want its value.

set score to 0
set name to "Sam"
say name, score
Changing it
Use `set` again to give it a new value, or `add` and `subtract` to change a number.

set score to 10
add 5 to score
subtract 1 from score
say score     # 14
Good names
Names use letters, numbers and `_`, and can't start with a number: `score`, `player_2` and `highScore` are fine, `2player` isn't. Capitals matter: `Score` and `score` are different.

set player_2 to 5
say player_2
One kind of value each
A variable keeps the same kind of value all the way through: if `score` holds a number, it can't hold text later. (A whole number can become a decimal, though.)

set total to 0
add 0.5 to total
say total     # 0.5

units.title: Maths
units.goal: Add, subtract, multiply, divide and more.
pages: The four sums
`+` adds, `-` subtracts, `*` multiplies and `/` divides. `/` always gives a decimal: `7 / 2` is `3.5`.

say 3 + 4
say 10 - 3
say 6 * 7
say 7 / 2
Which goes first
Like in school maths, `*` and `/` are done before `+` and `-`. Brackets go first of all.
Whole-number dividing
`//` divides and rounds down to a whole number. `mod` (or `%`) gives what's left over: the remainder. `7 // 2` is `3` and `7 mod 2` is `1`.

say 17 // 5     # 3
say 17 mod 5    # 2
Powers
`^` is a power: `2 ^ 3` is `2 * 2 * 2`, which is `8`.

challenge.task: A pizza has 8 slices and 3 friends share it equally. Say how many whole slices each gets (use `//`), then how many are left over (use `mod`).
challenge.starter:

units.title: Text
units.goal: Join text, put values inside it, and look at its letters.
pages: Values inside text
Put any value inside text with `{ }`. You can even do sums in there.

set name to "Sam"
set age to 12
say "{name} is {age}"
say "Next year: {age + 1}"
Joining text
`+` joins text together. Numbers are turned into text when they're joined to it.

say "Hello, " + "world"
say "Score: " + 100
Letters
`word[1]` is the first letter (counting starts at 1). `length of word` is how many letters it has.

set word to "hello"
say word[1]
say length of word
Capitals and searching
`uppercase` and `lowercase` change the letters. `contains(text, part)` says if the part is in it.

say uppercase("hi")
say contains("hello", "ell")

challenge.task: Set `pet` to "Rex" and `legs` to 4, then say `Rex has 4 legs` using `{ }`.
challenge.starter:

set legs to 4
challenge.solution:

units.title: Asking questions
units.goal: Let the person using your program type answers.
pages: ask
`ask("question")` shows the question, waits for the person to type an answer and press Enter, and gives back what they typed, as text. In Flaux Studio, type it in the box under the Output.

set name to ask("What's your name?")
say "Hi {name}!"
Numbers from answers
What `ask` gives back is always text, even if they typed a number. `number(...)` turns it into a decimal number and `whole(...)` into a whole number, so you can do sums with it.

set age to whole(ask("How old are you?"))
say "Next year you'll be {age + 1}"
Checking the answer
`is_number(text)` says if the text is a number, so you can ask again if it isn't.

set answer to ask("Pick a number")
if is_number(answer)
    say number(answer) * 2
else
    say "That isn't a number"
end

say "Yum, " + food

units.title: Making choices
units.goal: Do different things depending on a check.
pages: if
The lines between `if` and `end` only run when the check is true.

set score to 120
if score > 100
    say "Amazing!"
end
else
`else` runs when the check is false. `else if` adds another check. Only one part runs: the first one whose check is true.

set score to 70
if score > 100
    say "Amazing!"
else if score > 50
    say "Good job"
else
    say "Keep trying"
end
Comparing

`=` (or `is`) checks if two things are equal, `!=` (or `is not`) if they're different. `<`, `>`, `<=` and `>=` compare sizes, and you can write them in words: `is less than`, `is more than`, `is at most`, `is at least`.

set lives to 0
if lives = 0
    say "Game over"
end
Indenting
Indenting the inside of an `if` (Tab) isn't needed, but it shows at a glance what's inside. Every `if` ends with its own `end`.

set age to 15
if age >= 13
    if age <= 19
        say "teenager"
    end
end

challenge.task: `temperature` is 30. Say `Hot` if it's more than 25, otherwise say `Not hot`.
challenge.solution:

units.title: and, or, not
pages: true and false
A check like `3 > 2` gives `true` or `false`. You can say it, or keep it in a variable.

say 3 > 2
set finished to false
say finished
and
`a and b` is true only when both are true.

set age to 15
if age >= 13 and age <= 19
    say "teenager"
end
or
`a or b` is true when at least one of them is true. Each side must be a whole check: `name = "Sam" or name = "Bo"`, not `name = "Sam" or "Bo"`.

set name to "Bo"
if name = "Sam" or name = "Bo"
    say "Hi, friend"
end
not
`not` turns true into false and false into true.

set finished to false
if not finished
    say "still going"
end

units.title: Loops
pages: Repeat a number of times
The lines between `repeat ... times` and `end` run that many times.

repeat 3 times
    say "hip hip hooray"
end
Counting
`repeat with i from 1 to 5` runs with `i` being 1, then 2, up to 5. Add `by` to count in steps (a minus step counts down).

repeat with i from 1 to 5
    say i
end
repeat with i from 10 to 0 by -5
    say i
end
Going through things
`repeat with item in ...` goes through every item of a list, or every letter of a text.

repeat with fruit in ["apple", "pear"]
    say fruit
end
While and until
`repeat while` keeps going as long as its check is true. `repeat until` keeps going until its check becomes true.

set lives to 3
repeat while lives > 0
    say lives
    subtract 1 from lives
end
stop and skip
Inside a loop, `stop` leaves it straight away, and `skip` jumps to the next time round.

repeat with i from 1 to 10
    if i = 4
        stop
    end
    say i
end

repeat with i from 1 to 10
    add i to total

units.title: Lists
units.goal: Keep many values together in order.
pages: Making a list
A list is values in square brackets. Every item is the same kind.

set nums to [3, 1, 4]
set names to ["Sam", "Bo"]
say nums
Items
`nums[1]` is the first item: counting starts at 1, like on your fingers. Change an item with `set nums[1] to ...`.

set nums to [3, 1, 4]
say nums[1]
set nums[1] to 100
say nums
Adding and counting
`add x to list` puts an item on the end. `length of list` is how many items it has, and `contains(list, x)` says if it's there.

set nums to [3, 1]
add 4 to nums
say length of nums
say contains(nums, 4)
Many copies
`5 copies of 0` makes `[0, 0, 0, 0, 0]`. Start an empty list with `[]`.

set scores to 3 copies of 0
set names to []
add "Sam" to names
say scores, names

units.title: Functions
pages: Your own instruction
`function name(inputs)` ... `end` makes a new instruction. Use it by writing its name with the inputs in brackets.

function greet(name)
    say "Hello, {name}!"
end

greet("Sam")
greet("Bo")
Giving back a value
`return` gives a value back to where the function was used, and leaves the function.

function area(width, height)
    return width * height
end

say area(3, 4)
Only their own inputs

A function only sees its inputs and its own variables. To use a value from outside, pass it in; to change it, give back the new value. (Lists are different: changing a list you were given changes the original.)

function lose_life(lives)
    return lives - 1
end

set lives to 3
set lives to lose_life(lives)
say lives
Calling itself
A function can use itself. This is called recursion.

function factorial(n)
    if n <= 1
        return 1
    end
    return n * factorial(n - 1)
end

say factorial(5)

challenge.task: Write a function `triple(n)` that gives back `n * 3`, and use it to say `triple(7)`.
challenge.solution:
function triple(n)
    return n * 3
end

say triple(7)

units.title: Built-in functions
units.goal: Use the instructions that come with Flaux.
pages: Rounding
`round(x)` rounds to the nearest whole number, `floor(x)` rounds down and `ceil(x)` rounds up.

say round(2.6)
say floor(2.6)
say ceil(2.1)
Biggest, smallest, size
`min(...)` and `max(...)` give the smallest and the biggest. `abs(x)` takes away the minus sign. `sqrt(x)` is the square root.

say max(3, 9, 4)
say min(3, 9, 4)
say abs(-5)
say sqrt(16)
Changing kinds
`text(x)` turns a value into text, `number(t)` turns text into a decimal and `whole(x)` into a whole number (it drops what's after the point: `whole(3.9)` is `3`).

say text(42) + "!"
say number("3.5") * 2
say whole(3.9)
How far
`distance(x1, y1, x2, y2)` says how far apart two points are.
say distance(0, 0, 3, 4)

units.title: Random and waiting
units.goal: Surprise the player, and take your time.
pages: Random numbers
`random(1, 6)` gives a random whole number from 1 to 6, both included: like a dice.
say random(1, 6)
Random items
`random(list)` picks a random item from the list.
say random(["rock", "paper", "scissors"])
Waiting
`wait` pauses. Glue a unit to the number: `s` seconds, `m` minutes, `h` hours, `d` days. For a variable, write the unit as a word: `wait delay seconds`. `wait 5` alone is a mistake: 5 what?

say "Ready..."
wait 1s
say "Go!"

units.title: Drawing
units.goal: Open a window and draw shapes and text.
pages: The window
`window(800, 600)` opens a window 800 pixels wide and 600 tall. Places are measured from the top-left corner: `x` goes right and `y` goes DOWN.
window(800, 600, "My picture")
Shapes
`rect(x, y, width, height, colour)` draws a rectangle from its top-left corner. `circle(x, y, radius, colour)` draws a circle around its centre. There's also `line`, `triangle` and `dot`.

window(400, 300)
clear("sky")
rect(0, 250, 400, 50, "green")
circle(320, 60, 30, "yellow")
Words
`write(value, x, y, colour, size)` draws text in the window.

window(400, 300)
write("Hello!", 20, 20, "white", 4)
Colours
Use a colour name like `"red"` or `"dark green"`, `rgb(255, 136, 0)` (red, green and blue from 0 to 255) or a code like `"#ff8800"`.

challenge.task: Draw a house: a square for the walls and a triangle for the roof.

units.title: Games
units.goal: Make things move, with the keyboard and the mouse.
pages: The game loop
A game draws a new picture many times a second. Put the drawing in `repeat forever` and end each picture with `show()`. `show()` waits so the loop runs 60 times a second.

window(400, 300)
set x to 0
repeat forever
    add 2 to x
    clear()
    circle(x, 150, 20, "red")
    show()
end
Keys
`key_down("left")` is true while the key is held: use it for smooth moving. `key_pressed("space")` is true only on the frame the key goes down: use it for jumping or firing.

window(400, 300)
set x to 200
repeat forever
    if key_down("left")
        subtract 4 from x
    end
    if key_down("right")
        add 4 to x
    end
    clear()
    rect(x, 250, 40, 20, "blue")
    show()
end
The mouse
`mouse_x()` and `mouse_y()` say where the mouse is. `mouse_down()` is true while the left button is held, and `mouse_clicked()` only on the frame of a click. Add `"right"` for the right button.

window(400, 300)
repeat forever
    clear()
    circle(mouse_x(), mouse_y(), 10, "yellow")
    show()
end
Did they touch?
Two circles touch when the distance between their centres is less than their two radiuses added together.

set score to 0
set px to 100
set py to 100
set cx to 120
set cy to 110
if distance(px, py, cx, cy) < 20 + 10
    add 1 to score
end
say score

units.title: Pictures and sound
units.goal: Draw picture files and make beeps.
pages: Pictures
`image("ship.png", x, y)` draws a picture file with its top-left corner at `x, y`. Put the file in the same folder as your program. PNG, JPG, BMP and GIF work.

window(400, 300)
image("ship.png", 100, 100)
Bigger, flipped, turned
Give a width and height to stretch it. A minus width or height flips it. A last number turns it that many degrees.
Beeps
`beep(pitch, seconds)` plays a note. 440 is the note A; bigger numbers are higher. Beeps play one after another, so several make a tune.

challenge.task: Play a little tune of three beeps that go up.

units.title: 3D
units.goal: Build a 3D world with shapes, a camera and light.
pages: Three directions
In 3D, `x` goes right, `y` goes UP and `z` comes towards you. Sizes are in steps: a cube of size 1 is one step wide. Every shape is placed by its middle.

window(800, 600)
repeat forever
    cube(0, 0.5, 0, 1, "red")
    show()
end
Shapes
`cube`, `box`, `ball`, `cylinder`, `cone` and `plane` (a flat floor). The last input is the paint: a colour, a picture file or a shader.

window(800, 600)
repeat forever
    plane(0, 0, 0, 20, 20, "green")
    ball(0, 1, 0, 1, "orange")
    show()
end
The camera
`camera(x, y, z, look_x, look_y, look_z)` is where you see from and the point you look at.

window(800, 600)
repeat forever
    camera(5, 4, 5, 0, 0, 0)
    cube(0, 0.5, 0, 1, "red")
    show()
end
Sky, sun and lamps
`sky(colour)` paints the sky, `sun(x, y, z)` is where sunlight comes from (it makes shadows), `light(...)` adds a lamp and `fog(distance)` fades things far away.

window(800, 600)
repeat forever
    sky("navy")
    sun(0, 0, 0)
    light(0, 2, 0, "orange")
    plane(0, 0, 0, 20, 20, "gray")
    show()
end

challenge.task: Make a little 3D scene: a green floor with a tower of 3 cubes on it.
challenge.starter:

repeat forever
    plane(0, 0, 0, 20, 20, "green")
    show()
end
challenge.solution:

        cube(0, i - 0.5, 0, 1, "red")
    end

end

units.title: Shaders
pages: A tiny program for every pixel
A shader runs on the graphics card, once for every pixel, and gives back a colour. Write it outside any function, with `shader name` ... `end`.

shader glow
    set brightness to sin(time * 3) * 0.5 + 0.5
    return rgb(255 * brightness, 120, 40)
end
Using it
Use a shader's name in place of a colour on a shape, or for the whole screen with `effect(name)` before `show()`.

shader stripes
    if floor(y * 4) mod 2 = 0
        return "white"
    end
    return "red"
end

window(800, 600)
repeat forever
    cube(0, 0.5, 0, 1, stripes)
    show()
end
What a shader knows

On shapes: `x`, `y`, `z` (the point), `u`, `v` (where on the face) and `time`. In `effect`: `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` and the pixel's `red`, `green` and `blue`. Shaders can't use lists, text, `say` or your own functions.

challenge.task: Make a shader that paints a cube in a colour that changes with `time`, and use it.
challenge.solution:
shader pulse
    return rgb(128 + 127 * sin(time), 50, 200)
end

window(800, 600)
repeat forever
    cube(0, 0.5, 0, 1, pulse)
    show()
end

units.title: Finding mistakes
units.goal: Read Flaux's messages and fix your program.
pages: Flaux helps
When something's wrong, Flaux Studio underlines the line, says what's wrong in plain words and often has an Apply fix button. Read the message: it usually says exactly what to change.

set score to 10
say scroe     # I don't know what `scroe` is. Did you mean `score`?
The usual suspects
A missing `end`, a misspelled name, a missing quote `"`, `wait 5` without a unit, or `x = 5` instead of `set x to 5`.

set x to 5
if x > 3
    say "big"
end
Problems while running
Some problems only show up while the program runs, like dividing by zero or asking for item 10 of a list with 3. The program stops and the line it stopped on is lit up.

set nums to [1, 2, 3]
say nums[3]     # fine: nums[10] would stop the program
